items.source: At the time of events giving rise to this complaint, Complainant worked as a Full-time Mail Handler Equipment Operator at the Agency’s Morgan Processing and Distribution Center facility in New York, New York. On November 18, 2021, Complainant filed an EEO complaint alleging that the Agency discriminated against her on the bases of sex (female), disability (physical), and reprisal for prior protected EEO activity under Title VII and the Rehabilitation Act when: 1. On June 25, 2021, and ongoing, she was denied overtime work within her limitations; 2. On July 19, 2021, she was verbally abused by a coworker and no action was taken; 2 3. Beginning on August 1, 2021, and ongoing, she was micromanaged and assigned to either the rewrap section or city manual section and/or confronted about her job duties; and 4. On August 31, 2021, her request for a temporary change of schedule was denied. After its investigation into the complaint, the Agency indicated that, on April 5, 2022, it transmitted to Complainant and her non-attorney representative a copy of the report of investigation (ROI) and notice of her right to request a hearing (Notice) before an EEOC AJ. On April 5, 2022, the Agency emailed Complainant and her representative, stating that a copy of the final ROI was available for download for a period of 30 days and requesting that the parties send an email confirming receipt. CF at 98-103. The record contains an April 5, 2022, message reflecting that the message was relayed to Complainant and her representative but that the destination server did not send a delivery notification. CF at 97. The Agency initially accepted the following for investigation: “On July 20, 2021, you were verbally abused by a supervisor and no action was taken.” CF at 60. Complainant clarified during the investigation that this incident occurred on July 19, 2021, that it was a coworker who verbally abused her, and that, when she reported it to supervisors, nothing was done about it. CF at 205-08. Also on April 5, 2022, the Agency provided Complainant and her representative 3 with a copy of documents that were submitted after the completion of the investigative file, asking that they be added to Complainant’s copy of the recently submitted file. CF at 85-96. The documents consist of an Acting Supervisor’s investigative affidavit, completed on March 28, 2022, and the Acting Supervisor’s Litigation Hold Notice, which was signed on March 31, 2022. CF at 86-95. In the affidavit, the Acting Supervisor stated that he had no organizational relationship to Complainant during the relevant time and that he was not at the facility on July 20, 2021. CF at 86-93. On May 17, 2022, the Agency again emailed Complainant and her non- attorney representative, notifying them that an electronic copy of the ROI would be available for download for a period of 30 days. CF at 82-83. The record contains a May 17, 2022, message reflecting that the message was relayed to Complainant and her representative but that the destination server did not send a delivery notification. CF at 84. On May 31, 2022, Complainant mailed a hearing request to the Agency and to the Commission’s New York District Office. CF at 40-42. The Agency stamped the mailing envelope and the hearing request form as received on June 6, 2022. CF at 40, 42. Complainant included a May 28, 2022, letter with her hearing request, in which she stated that, after receiving the Acting Supervisor’s affidavit in April 2022, she wanted to refute his response that he was not present on the date of the incident and requested a copy of his Employee Everything Report from the Agency. CF at 41. According to Complainant, on May 18, 2022, she called an EEO Services Analyst to refute the Acting Supervisor’s statement, and the EEO Services Analyst told her that her case was closed on May 1, 2022. CF at 41. Complainant averred that she asked how her case could be closed if she and her representative had not been notified or received a copy of the ROI. CF at 41. Complainant stated that the EEO Services Analyst told her that she could request a hearing but should attach a letter stating that she found out her case was closed on May 18, 2022. CF at 41. It appears that these documents were provided to Complainant and her representative via first class mail. CF at 85. On June 2, 2022, the Agency issued a final decision. The Agency stated that it was issuing the decision pursuant to 29 C.F.R. § 1614.110(b) because Complainant did not request a hearing within the time frame provided in 29 C.F.R. § 1614.108(f). The decision concluded that Complainant failed to prove that the Agency subjected her to discrimination as alleged. On June 10, 2022, the EEOC’s New York District Office received Complainant’s hearing request, which was docketed as Hearing No. 520- 2022-00326X. On June 15, 2022, Complainant filed the instant appeal. On July 6, 2022, the Agency provided Complainant and her representative with documents that were submitted after the completion of the investigative file, asking that they be added to Complainant’s copy of the recently submitted file. CF at 1-10. The document is an updated June 7, 2022, affidavit from the Acting Supervisor. CF at 2-10. The Acting Supervisor stated that, during the timeframe of the complaint, his organizational relationship with Complainant was Acting Supervisor. CF at 2. The Acting Supervisor stated that he was not present when the coworker verbally abused Complainant on July 19, 2021, and that he did not know if Complainant or anyone acting on her behalf reported any harassment. CF at 4-9. On November 29, 2022, an EEOC AJ issued an order dismissing Complainant’s hearing request, noting that the Agency had already issued a final decision, which Complainant had appealed.

# CASE FILE SUMMARY

**Complainant Status:** Full-time Mail Handler Equipment Operator at Agency's Morgan Processing and Distribution Center, New York, New York

**Complaint Filing Date:** November 18, 2021

**Bases of Complaint:** Sex (female), disability (physical), and reprisal for prior protected EEO activity under Title VII and the Rehabilitation Act

**Allegations:**
1. On June 25, 2021, and ongoing: Denied overtime work within her limitations
2. On July 19, 2021: Verbally abused by a coworker; no action taken (CF at 205-08)
3. Beginning August 1, 2021, and ongoing: Micromanaged and assigned to rewrap section or city manual section and/or confronted about job duties
4. On August 31, 2021: Request for temporary change of schedule denied

**Initial Allegation as Accepted:** "On July 20, 2021, you were verbally abused by a supervisor and no action was taken." (CF at 60)

**Clarification During Investigation:** Complainant clarified that the incident occurred on July 19, 2021, that it was a coworker (not a supervisor) who verbally abused her, and that supervisors took no action when she reported it. (CF at 205-08)

**Investigation Completion and ROI Transmission:**
- **April 5, 2022:** Agency transmitted ROI and Notice of right to hearing to Complainant and her non-attorney representative (CF at 98-103). Email stated ROI available for download for 30 days and requested confirmation of receipt; destination server did not send delivery notification. (CF at 97)

**Post-Investigation Documents Submitted:**
- **April 5, 2022:** Agency provided Acting Supervisor's investigative affidavit (completed March 28, 2022) and Litigation Hold Notice (signed March 31, 2022) (CF at 85-96, 86-95). Acting Supervisor stated he had no organizational relationship to Complainant during relevant time and was not at facility on July 20, 2021. (CF at 86-93)

- **May 17, 2022:** Agency again emailed Complainant and her non-attorney representative notifying them ROI available for download for 30 days; destination server did not send delivery notification. (CF at 82-84)

Documents appear to have been provided via first class mail. (CF at 85)

**Hearing Request:**
- **May 31, 2022:** Complainant mailed hearing request to Agency and Commission's New York District Office (CF at 40-42)
- **June 6, 2022:** Agency received hearing request (stamped on mailing envelope and form) (CF at 40, 42)
- **May 28, 2022 Letter:** Included with hearing request, Complainant refuted Acting Supervisor's affidavit statement that he was not present on date of incident and requested Employee Everything Report from Agency (CF at 41)
- **May 18, 2022 Phone Call:** According to Complainant, she called EEO Services Analyst to refute Acting Supervisor's statement; EEO Services Analyst told her case was closed on May 1, 2022 (CF at 41). Complainant asked how case could be closed if she and representative had not been notified or received ROI (CF at 41). EEO Services Analyst told her she could request hearing but should attach letter stating she found out case was closed on May 18, 2022 (CF at 41)

**Agency Final Decision:**
- **June 2, 2022:** Agency issued final decision pursuant to 29 C.F.R. § 1614.110(b), citing failure to request hearing within timeframe provided in 29 C.F.R. § 1614.108(f). Agency concluded Complainant failed to prove Agency subjected her to discrimination as alleged.

**Post-Decision Documents:**
- **July 6, 2022:** Agency provided updated June 7, 2022, affidavit from Acting Supervisor (CF at 1-10). Acting Supervisor stated his organizational relationship with Complainant during complaint timeframe was Acting Supervisor (CF at 2). Acting Supervisor stated he was not present when coworker verbally abused Complainant on July 19, 2021, and did not know if Complainant or anyone acting on her behalf reported any harassment (CF at 4-9)

**Commission Action:**
- **June 10, 2022:** EEOC's New York District Office received Complainant's hearing request; docketed as Hearing No. 520-2022-00326X
- **June 15, 2022:** Complainant filed instant appeal
- **November 29, 2022:** EEOC AJ issued order dismissing Complainant's hearing request, noting Agency had already issued final decision, which Complainant had appealed

# Case File Summary

## Parties and Claims

- **Complaint filed:** November 18, 2021. Complainant alleged discrimination based on sex (female), disability (physical), and reprisal for prior protected EEO activity, under Title VII and the Rehabilitation Act.

  2. On July 19, 2021, a coworker verbally abused her and no action was taken.
  3. Beginning August 1, 2021, and ongoing, she was micromanaged, assigned to either the rewrap section or city manual section, and/or confronted about her job duties.
  4. On August 31, 2021, her request for a temporary schedule change was denied.

## Claim 2 Clarification
- The Agency initially accepted the claim as: "On July 20, 2021, you were verbally abused by a supervisor and no action was taken." (CF at 60.)
- Complainant clarified during the investigation that the incident occurred on July 19, 2021, that a coworker was the abuser, and that supervisors did nothing when she reported it. (CF at 205-08.)

- **Agency's account:** The Agency indicated that on April 5, 2022, it sent Complainant and her non-attorney representative the report of investigation (ROI) and notice of the right to request a hearing before an EEOC AJ.
- **April 5, 2022 email:** The Agency said the final ROI was available for download for 30 days and asked for confirmation of receipt. (CF at 98-103.) A message dated April 5, 2022, shows the email was relayed but the destination server sent no delivery notification. (CF at 97.)
- **May 17, 2022 email:** The Agency again emailed both, saying an electronic ROI copy would be available for 30 days. (CF at 82-83.) The May 17, 2022 message shows it was relayed but no delivery notification was sent. (CF at 84.)

## Supplemental Documents
- **April 5, 2022:** The Agency also sent Complainant and her representative documents submitted after the investigative file was completed, asking that they be added to her copy. (CF at 85-96.) They appear to have been sent by first class mail. (CF at 85.) The documents are:
  - The Acting Supervisor's investigative affidavit, completed March 28, 2022.
  - The Acting Supervisor's Litigation Hold Notice, signed March 31, 2022. (CF at 86-95.)
- **Acting Supervisor's statement (March 28, 2022 affidavit):** He said he had no organizational relationship to Complainant during the relevant time and was not at the facility on July 20, 2021. (CF at 86-93.)
- **July 6, 2022:** The Agency sent a further document, an updated affidavit from the Acting Supervisor dated June 7, 2022. (CF at 1-10.) In it, the Acting Supervisor stated:
  - His organizational relationship with Complainant during the complaint timeframe was Acting Supervisor. (CF at 2.)
  - He was not present when the coworker verbally abused Complainant on July 19, 2021.
  - He did not know whether Complainant or anyone on her behalf reported harassment. (CF at 4-9.)

## Hearing Request
- **May 31, 2022:** Complainant mailed a hearing request to the Agency and to the Commission's New York District Office. (CF at 40-42.)
- **Receipt:** The Agency stamped the envelope and the request form as received June 6, 2022. (CF at 40, 42.) The EEOC New York District Office received the request June 10, 2022, and docketed it as Hearing No. 520-2022-00326X.
- **Complainant's May 28, 2022 letter (CF at 41):**
  - After receiving the Acting Supervisor's affidavit in April 2022, she wanted to refute his statement that he was not present on the date of the incident. She requested his Employee Everything Report from the Agency.
  - By her account, on May 18, 2022, she called an EEO Services Analyst to refute the statement. The Analyst told her the case had been closed on May 1, 2022.
  - She said she asked how the case could be closed when she and her representative had not been notified of or received the ROI.
  - She said the Analyst told her she could request a hearing but should attach a letter stating she learned on May 18, 2022, that the case was closed.

- **Agency final decision (June 2, 2022):** The Agency issued it under 29 C.F.R. § 1614.110(b), stating that Complainant did not request a hearing within the time frame in 29 C.F.R. § 1614.108(f). It concluded Complainant failed to prove discrimination as alleged. The record names no individual decision-maker.
- **Appeal:** Complainant filed the instant appeal on June 15, 2022.
- **EEOC AJ order (November 29, 2022):** An EEOC AJ dismissed the hearing request, noting that the Agency had already issued a final decision, which Complainant had appealed.

## Notes for the File
- The record does not state the Agency's reasoning on Complainant's hearing request or any response to her May 28, 2022 letter. It also does not state the outcome of the appeal.
- The record shows no delivery notifications for either email transmission of the ROI (CF at 97, 84).
- The Acting Supervisor's two affidavits differ on his organizational relationship to Complainant.

items.source: At the time of events giving rise to this complaint, Complainant worked as a Level 1 City Carrier at the Agency’s Meadow Mesa Station facility in North Las Vegas, Nevada. On February 25, 2023, Complainant filed an EEO complaint alleging that the Agency discriminated against him and subjected him to harassment on the basis of age (born 1973) when: 1. On August 30, 2022, Complainant was put on Emergency Placement. 2. On September 14, 2022, Complainant was suspended. 3. On September 20, 2022, one of Complainant’s supervisors followed him to the bathroom, yelled at him to get back to work, and threatened him with discipline. 4. On September 24, 2022, one of Complainant’s supervisors accused him of not fastening his seatbelt before starting the engine. 5. On November 1, 2022, Complainant was escorted out of the facility. The Agency accepted these claims and conducted an investigation which produced the following evidence. Claim 1 In his investigative affidavit, Complainant stated that on August 30, 2022, he asked one of his supervisors, S1, to sign or initial his copy of a request for Union time. Complainant stated that S1 said she would do so later, and he then asked her why she could not just sign or initial the request at that time. Complainant stated that S1 repeated she would do so later and that he needed to get back to work. At this point, Complainant stated that Postmaster (PM) asked him what was going on, and after explaining the situation, PM asked him whether S1 gave him instructions to get back to work. Complainant stated that he said yes, and then PM asked him whether he was refusing to do so. Complainant stated that he said he was not refusing to get back to work but wanted to understand why he was being held to policy and not S1. After leaving the office area, and while he was in the locker room, Complainant stated that PM walked in and asked him why he had not left yet. PM further questioned what Complainant was doing for the last hour, and when Complainant tried to explain, Complainant stated that PM interrupted him, yelled at him, and leaned over him in an attempt to intimidate him. After this exchange, and while Complainant was still in the locker room, Complainant stated that PM walked in again and told him he needed to deliver to the apartments that day. Complainant stated that he asked PM whether he needed to finish the apartments that day because it would put him over eight hours. Complainant stated PM then accused him of failing to follow instructions, refused his request for a union steward, demanded his badge, yelled at him to clean out his locker, and threatened to call the authorities to have him removed from the premises. In his affidavit, PM stated that he observed Complainant engaging in several time-wasting practices and was given instructions which he failed to follow. PM further stated that in alignment with Agency policy, Complainant was placed on Emergency Placement (EP) in an off- duty status without pay for failure to follow instructions. With respect to Complainant’s intimidation claim, PM stated that the claim was ridiculous, and since having COVID, he does not get close to any employee. PM also stated that a union steward was not available, and Complainant was told he could speak with his union steward, but he had to leave the facility immediately. In her affidavit, S1 confirmed that she asked Complainant around three times to deliver his route, but he did not listen to her. S1 stated that Complainant then became argumentative with PM. With respect to Complainant’s intimidation claim, S1 stated that she did not have any knowledge of what might have occurred in the men’s locker room. S1 further stated that no employee placed on EP was allowed to have a conversation with the union before leaving the premises. Complainant stated that his age was a factor when he was placed on EP because he was tasked with trying to complete an overburdened route within eight hours and was compared constantly to younger carriers. Complainant did not have any specific examples of similarly situated employees outside his protected class who were treated more favorably under similar circumstances. Claim 2 In his affidavit, Complainant stated that on September 14, 2022, after completing vehicle inspection and as he was loading his mail truck, S1 and his other supervisor, herein identified as S2, approached him and S2 demanded his badge. Complainant stated that S2 explained he was being walked out because he did not fasten his seatbelt before starting the vehicle and that he got out of the driver’s seat while the engine was running. Complainant stated that he then asked for a union steward but S2 denied his request. Complainant further stated that it was his understanding that Section 812. of Handbook M-41 specified that seatbelts were to be worn at all times the vehicle was in motion. The record reflects that Complainant was again placed on EP in an off-duty status without pay. While Complainant received a Notice of 14-Day Suspension Letter on September 22, 2022, the letter cites to incident(s) of failing to follow instructions on August 30, 2022, as the reason for Complainant’s suspension. Report of Investigation (ROI) at 00192-00193. In his affidavit, S2 stated that Complainant was observed exiting the mail truck and walking in front of it while the engine was running. S2 stated that this was a safety violation, and it was Agency policy for seatbelts to be worn at all times while operating a vehicle. S2 further stated that since Complainant was immediately placed on EP, he had to contact the union off postal property. In her affidavit, S1 stated that she had no knowledge of this incident since she was not present when it occurred. Complainant stated that he did not think his age factored into this incident and did not have any specific examples of similarly situated employees outside his protected class who were treated more favorably under similar circumstances. Claim 3 In his affidavit, Complainant stated that on September 20, 2022, S2 followed him into the bathroom two separate times and yelled at him. Complainant further stated that S2 threatened to discipline him. S2 denied raising his voice to Complainant, and stated that if he followed him, it was because of Complainant’s performance. S2 further stated that rather than washing up in the bathroom, Complainant was spending a long time in the locker room and doing something in his locker. Complainant stated that he believed his age was a factor when he was purportedly yelled at and threatened with discipline because now that he is older, he has to use the bathroom more often than he did when he was younger. Complainant did not have any specific examples of similarly situated employees outside his protected class who were treated more favorably under similar circumstances. Claim 4 In his affidavit, Complainant stated that on September 24, 2022, he started the engine of his mail truck and was fastening his seatbelt when S2 walked up to the passenger-side window and yelled at him for not fastening his seatbelt before he started the engine. Citing to Section 812. of Handbook M-41, Complainant stated that S2 improperly demanded that seatbelts are to be fastened before the engine is started as opposed to before the vehicle is shifted into gear and put into motion. Complainant further stated that S1 walked over to them and S2 asked her whether she saw anything wrong. Complainant stated that S1 said no and while S1 and S2 were talking to each other and making calls, he called the National Association of Letter Carriers (NALC) office. Complainant stated that someone from NALC confirmed his understanding of the Agency’s seatbelt policy, and when he asked the NALC officer to repeat what he said to S1 and S2, S1 told him it was not necessary, and he could go and deliver his route. Complainant stated that S1 also told him he had to follow all supervisor instructions and starting right then, he needed to fasten his seatbelt before he started the engine. S2 stated that he thought seatbelts needed to be fastened before starting a vehicle. S2 stated that he called safety and was told that it was not a written Agency policy. S2 further stated that he informed Complainant of this conversation and Complainant was then allowed to continue to his route. S1 confirmed that S2 called her over and asked whether she observed Complainant doing anything wrong. S1 stated that she did not, and ultimately told Complainant to follow the instructions of his supervisor. When asked if the requirement to fasten seatbelts before starting a vehicle applied to all employees going forward, S1 stated that she was not sure whether the request was sent to all carriers or if other carriers already fastened their seatbelts before starting their vehicles. S1 further stated that the relevant conversation was between S2 and Complainant. Complainant stated that he did not think his age factored into this incident and did not have any specific examples of similarly situated employees outside his protected class who were treated more favorably under similar circumstances. Claim 5 In his affidavit, Complainant stated that on November 1, 2022, he gave S1 a doctor’s note for 30 days of no overtime due to repetitive motion pain in his right shoulder. Complainant stated that S1 told him she did not need to honor his doctor’s note. Later that evening, Complainant returned with undelivered mail and clocked out. Complainant stated that S1 told him he needed to continue delivering the mail until he finished his route. Complainant stated that he reminded S1 of his doctor’s note and that he was unable to work overtime. Complainant stated that S1 asked him whether he was refusing to follow instructions. Complainant further stated that he told S1 he did not have to follow unsafe supervisor instructions, and ignoring his doctor’s note and demanding he work overtime did not seem safe to him. 2 Complainant stated that S1 then demanded his badge, and he was escorted off the premises. The record reflects that Complainant was again placed on EP in an off-duty status without pay, effective November 2, 2022. S1 stated that Complainant told her, based on union advice, that he could bring his mail back and he did not have to listen to management. S1 stated that she asked Complainant three times to finish his route, but Complainant kept reiterating what the union told him. S1 stated that, while the union could provide guidance, she told Complainant that he had to follow supervisor instruction. S1 further explained that she sent Complainant’s medical documentation to Occupational Health Management (OHM) for guidance, and OHM advised her that Complainant could finish his route that day. S1 stated that OHM advised her that they were looking into the matter and to wait for an update as to whether the doctor’s note needed to be honored as a limited duty job offer, or if it needed to be a light duty request that required submission to the PM for approval. Complainant stated that he believed his age was a factor when he was escorted off the premises because he was expected to finish an overburdened route, and now that he is older, he has noticed that he does not recover from pain and injuries as quickly as he did when he was younger. Complainant did not have any specific examples of similarly situated employees outside his protected class who were treated more favorably under similar circumstances. At the conclusion of the investigation, the Agency provided Complainant with a copy of the report of investigation and notice of his right to request a hearing before an Equal Employment Opportunity Commission Administrative Judge (AJ). Disability was not a basis raised in Complainant’s complaint. Complainant timely requested a hearing. When Complainant did not object, the AJ assigned to the case granted the Agency’s December 14, 2023, motion for a decision without a hearing and issued a decision without a hearing on January 4, 2024. The Agency subsequently issued a final order adopting the AJ’s finding that Complainant failed to prove that the Agency subjected him to discrimination and harassment as alleged. The AJ found that the Agency's unrebutted facts served to establish nondiscriminatory reasons for its actions. The AJ noted, for example, that Complainant argued with his supervisors, wasted time on his phone in the locker room, neglected to fasten his seatbelt, and failed to turn his vehicle off when exiting. The AJ found that these predicates, which Complainant did not dispute, provided sufficient nondiscriminatory justification for the discipline and other actions management meted out. The AJ found that Complainant did not offer evidence that management made biased comments about his age or that they treated younger workers more favorably. As a result, the AJ found that no reasonable factfinder, even viewing the evidence in the light most favorable to Complainant, could conclude the Agency's actions were tainted by considerations of Complainant's age. The Agency subsequently issued a final order fully implementing the AJ’s decision. The instant appeal from Complainant followed.

S2 stated Complainant was observed exiting the mail truck and walking in front of it while the engine was running. S2 stated this was a safety violation and it was Agency policy for seatbelts to be worn at all times while operating a vehicle. S2 stated that since Complainant was immediately placed on EP, he had to contact the union off postal property.

*S1's Account (Affidavit):*
S1 stated she had no knowledge of this incident since she was not present when it occurred.

---

**Claim 3: Bathroom Incident – September 20, 2022**

*Complainant's Account (Affidavit):*
On September 20, 2022, S2 followed him into the bathroom two separate times and yelled at him. S2 threatened to discipline him.

Complainant believed his age was a factor because now that he is older, he has to use the bathroom more often than when he was younger. Complainant did not provide specific examples of similarly situated employees outside his protected class treated more favorably.

*S2's Account (Affidavit):*
S2 denied raising his voice to Complainant and stated that if he followed him, it was because of Complainant's performance. S2 stated that rather than washing up in the bathroom, Complainant was spending a long time in the locker room and doing something in his locker.

---

**Claim 4: Seatbelt Instruction – September 24, 2022**

*Complainant's Account (Affidavit):*
On September 24, 2022, Complainant started the engine of his mail truck and was fastening his seatbelt when S2 walked up to the passenger-side window and yelled at him for not fastening his seatbelt before he started the engine. Citing Section 812 of Handbook M-41, Complainant stated S2 improperly demanded that seatbelts be fastened before the engine is started as opposed to before the vehicle is shifted into gear and put into motion. S1 walked over and S2 asked her whether she saw anything wrong. S1 said no. While S1 and S2 were talking and making calls, Complainant called the National Association of Letter Carriers (NALC) office. Someone from NALC confirmed his understanding of the Agency's seatbelt policy. When Complainant asked the NALC officer to repeat what he said to S1 and S2, S1 told him it was not necessary and he could go deliver his route. S1 also told him he had to follow all supervisor instructions and starting right then, he needed to fasten his seatbelt before he started the engine.

Complainant stated he did not think his age factored into this incident and did not provide specific examples of similarly situated employees outside his protected class treated more favorably.

*S2's Account (Affidavit):*
S2 stated he thought seatbelts needed to be fastened before starting a vehicle. S2 stated he called safety and was told it was not a written Agency policy. S2 stated he informed Complainant of this conversation and Complainant was then allowed to continue to his route.

*S1's Account (Affidavit):*
S1 confirmed S2 called her over and asked whether she observed Complainant doing anything wrong. S1 stated she did not and ultimately told Complainant to follow the instructions of his supervisor. When asked if the requirement to fasten seatbelts before starting a vehicle applied to all employees going forward, S1 stated she was not sure whether the request was sent to all carriers or if other carriers already fastened their seatbelts before starting their vehicles. S1 stated the relevant conversation was between S2 and Complainant.

---

**Claim 5: Doctor's Note and Escorted Removal – November 1, 2022**

*Complainant's Account (Affidavit):*

Complainant reminded S1 of his doctor's note and that he was unable to work overtime. S1 asked him whether he was refusing to follow instructions. Complainant told S1 he did not have to follow unsafe supervisor instructions and that ignoring his doctor's note and demanding he work overtime did not seem safe to him. S1 demanded his badge and he was escorted off the premises.

Complainant was placed on EP in off-duty status without pay, effective November 2, 2022.

Complainant believed his age was a factor because he was expected to finish an overburdened route and, now that he is older, he has noticed he does not recover from pain and injuries as quickly as when he was younger. Note: Disability was not a basis raised in Complainant's complaint.

Complainant timely requested a hearing. When Complainant did not object, the AJ assigned to the case granted the Agency's December 14, 2023, motion for a decision without a hearing and issued a decision without a hearing on January 4, 2024.

---

## ADMINISTRATIVE JUDGE DECISION

**Decision Date:** January 4, 2024

**Decision-Maker:** Equal Employment Opportunity Commission Administrative Judge (AJ)

The AJ evaluated whether the Agency's unrebutted facts established nondiscriminatory reasons for its actions and whether Complainant offered evidence that management made biased comments about his age or treated younger workers more favorably.

**Findings:**

1. The Agency's unrebutted facts served to establish nondiscriminatory reasons for its actions.
2. Complainant argued with his supervisors, wasted time on his phone in the locker room, neglected to fasten his seatbelt, and failed to turn his vehicle off when exiting—predicates which Complainant did not dispute.
3. These predicates provided sufficient nondiscriminatory justification for the discipline and other actions management imposed.

5. No reasonable factfinder, even viewing the evidence in the light most favorable to Complainant, could conclude the Agency's actions were tainted by considerations of Complainant's age.

**Result:** The Agency failed to prove that the Agency subjected him to discrimination and harassment as alleged.

# Case File Summary

## Procedural Background
- Complainant was a Level 1 City Carrier at the Agency's Meadow Mesa Station in North Las Vegas, Nevada.
- On February 25, 2023, he filed an EEO complaint alleging age discrimination (born 1973) and harassment.
- The Agency accepted five claims and investigated.
- After the investigation, the Agency gave Complainant the report of investigation and notice of his right to request a hearing before an EEOC Administrative Judge (AJ).
- Complainant timely requested a hearing.
- Disability was not a basis raised in the complaint.
- The AJ granted the Agency's December 14, 2023 motion for a decision without a hearing, because Complainant did not object. The AJ issued the decision on January 4, 2024.
- The Agency then issued a final order adopting and fully implementing the AJ's decision. The record gives no date for the final order.
- Complainant appealed. The record gives no appeal date.

## Accepted Claims
1. August 30, 2022: placed on Emergency Placement (EP).
2. September 14, 2022: suspended.
3. September 20, 2022: a supervisor followed him to the bathroom, yelled at him to get back to work, and threatened discipline.
4. September 24, 2022: a supervisor accused him of not fastening his seatbelt before starting the engine.
5. November 1, 2022: escorted out of the facility.

## Evidence by Claim
The record identifies these individuals: S1 and S2 (supervisors) and PM (Postmaster).

**Claim 1 (EP, August 30, 2022)**
- *Complainant (affidavit):*
  - He asked S1 to sign or initial his copy of a Union time request. S1 said she would do so later and told him to get back to work.
  - PM asked whether he was refusing instructions. Complainant said he was not, but wanted to understand why he was held to policy and S1 was not.
  - In the locker room, PM questioned what he had been doing for the last hour, interrupted him, yelled, and leaned over him to intimidate him.
  - PM returned and told him to deliver to the apartments that day. Complainant asked whether this would put him over eight hours.
  - PM accused him of failing to follow instructions, refused his request for a union steward, demanded his badge, told him to clean out his locker, and threatened to call the authorities.
  - He believed age was a factor because he was given an overburdened route to finish within eight hours and was constantly compared to younger carriers.
  - He had no specific examples of similarly situated employees outside his protected class who were treated more favorably.
- *PM (affidavit):*
  - He observed several time-wasting practices, and Complainant failed to follow instructions.
  - Per Agency policy, Complainant was placed on EP, off duty without pay, for failure to follow instructions.
  - He called the intimidation claim ridiculous and said he does not get close to any employee since having COVID.
  - No union steward was available. Complainant was told he could speak with his steward but had to leave immediately.
- *S1 (affidavit):*
  - She asked Complainant about three times to deliver his route, and he did not listen. He then became argumentative with PM.
  - She had no knowledge of events in the men's locker room.
  - No employee placed on EP was allowed to speak with the union before leaving the premises.

**Claim 2 (suspension, September 14, 2022)**
- *Complainant (affidavit):*
  - S1 and S2 approached him as he loaded his mail truck, and S2 demanded his badge.
  - S2 said he was being walked out for not fastening his seatbelt before starting the vehicle and for leaving the driver's seat with the engine running.
  - S2 denied his request for a union steward.
  - He understood Section 812 of Handbook M-41 to require seatbelts only while the vehicle is in motion.
  - He did not think age factored into this incident and had no comparator examples.
- *The record:*
  - Complainant was again placed on EP, off duty without pay.
  - He received a Notice of 14-Day Suspension on September 22, 2022. The letter cites failure to follow instructions on August 30, 2022 as the reason. ROI at 00192-00193.
- *S2 (affidavit):*
  - He observed Complainant exit the truck and walk in front of it with the engine running.
  - He called this a safety violation and said Agency policy requires seatbelts at all times while operating a vehicle.
  - Because Complainant was placed on EP immediately, he had to contact the union off postal property.
- *S1 (affidavit):* She had no knowledge of the incident because she was not present.

**Claim 3 (bathroom, September 20, 2022)**
- *Complainant (affidavit):*
  - S2 followed him into the bathroom twice, yelled at him, and threatened discipline.
  - He believed age was a factor because, being older, he has to use the bathroom more often.
  - He had no comparator examples.
- *S2 (affidavit):*
  - He denied raising his voice.
  - He said that if he followed Complainant, it was because of Complainant's performance.
  - Complainant spent a long time in the locker room doing something in his locker rather than washing up.

**Claim 4 (seatbelt, September 24, 2022)**
- *Complainant (affidavit):*
  - He started the engine and was fastening his seatbelt when S2 yelled at him through the passenger window.
  - Citing Section 812 of Handbook M-41, he said S2 wrongly required fastening before the engine is started rather than before the vehicle is shifted into gear.
  - S1 told S2 she saw nothing wrong.
  - He called the National Association of Letter Carriers (NALC) office, and someone there confirmed his understanding of the policy.
  - S1 told him to deliver his route, to follow all supervisor instructions, and to fasten his seatbelt before starting the engine from then on.
  - He did not think age was a factor and had no comparator examples.
- *S2 (affidavit):*
  - He thought seatbelts needed to be fastened before starting a vehicle.
  - He called safety and was told this was not a written Agency policy.
  - He told Complainant this, and Complainant was allowed to proceed on his route.
- *S1 (affidavit):*
  - She confirmed S2 called her over and asked whether she saw anything wrong. She did not, and she told Complainant to follow his supervisor's instructions.
  - She was unsure whether the request was sent to all carriers or whether other carriers already fastened seatbelts before starting.
  - She said the relevant conversation was between S2 and Complainant.

**Claim 5 (escorted out, November 1, 2022)**
- *Complainant (affidavit):*
  - He gave S1 a doctor's note for 30 days of no overtime due to right shoulder repetitive motion pain. S1 said she did not need to honor it.
  - That evening he returned with undelivered mail and clocked out. S1 told him to keep delivering until he finished.
  - He cited the note and said that ignoring it and demanding overtime did not seem safe.
  - S1 asked whether he was refusing instructions, then demanded his badge, and he was escorted off the premises.
  - He believed age was a factor because he was expected to finish an overburdened route, and as an older worker he recovers more slowly from pain and injury.
  - He had no comparator examples.
- *The record:* Complainant was again placed on EP, off duty without pay, effective November 2, 2022.
- *S1 (affidavit):*
  - Complainant told her, on union advice, that he could bring his mail back and did not have to listen to management.
  - She asked him three times to finish his route and told him he had to follow supervisor instruction.
  - She sent his medical documentation to Occupational Health Management (OHM), which advised that he could finish his route that day.
  - OHM said it was looking into whether the note had to be honored as a limited duty job offer or treated as a light duty request requiring PM approval, and told her to wait for an update.

## Decision and Reasoning
- **Decision-makers:**
  - The AJ decided the case without a hearing on January 4, 2024.
  - The Agency adopted and fully implemented that decision in its final order.
- **Outcome:** Complainant failed to prove the Agency subjected him to discrimination and harassment as alleged.
- **Criteria applied (as stated in the record):**
  - Whether the Agency's unrebutted facts established nondiscriminatory reasons for its actions.
  - Whether Complainant offered evidence of biased age-related comments by management or more favorable treatment of younger workers.
  - Whether, viewing the evidence in the light most favorable to Complainant, a reasonable factfinder could conclude the Agency's actions were tainted by age considerations.
- **Responses considered:**
  - The AJ noted, as examples, that Complainant argued with supervisors, wasted time on his phone in the locker room, neglected to fasten his seatbelt, and failed to turn off his vehicle when exiting.
  - The AJ found these predicates undisputed and a sufficient nondiscriminatory justification for the discipline and other management actions.
  - The AJ found no evidence of biased age comments or more favorable treatment of younger workers, so no reasonable factfinder could find age-based taint.

## Items to Note
- The only record citation in the source is ROI at 00192-00193, for the suspension notice. The other statements are attributed to affidavits without page cites.
- Claim 2 is framed as a September 14, 2022 suspension. The record shows the September 14 action was an EP, and the 14-day suspension notice was received September 22, 2022, citing the August 30 incident.
- The AJ's reference to phone use in the locker room does not appear in the affidavit summaries above. S2 described only Complainant spending a long time in the locker room and doing something in his locker.

  - He asked S1 to sign or initial his copy of a Union time request. S1 said she would do so later and told him to get back to work.
  - PM asked whether he was refusing instructions. Complainant said he was not, but wanted to understand why he was held to policy and S1 was not.
  - In the locker room, PM questioned what he had been doing for the last hour, interrupted him, yelled, and leaned over him to intimidate him.
  - PM returned and told him to deliver to the apartments that day. Complainant asked whether this would put him over eight hours.
  - PM accused him of failing to follow instructions, refused his request for a union steward, demanded his badge, told him to clean out his locker, and threatened to call the authorities.
  - He believed age was a factor because he was given an overburdened route to finish within eight hours and was constantly compared to younger carriers.
  - He had no specific examples of similarly situated employees outside his protected class who were treated more favorably.
- *PM (affidavit):*
  - He observed several time-wasting practices, and Complainant failed to follow instructions.
  - Per Agency policy, Complainant was placed on EP, off duty without pay, for failure to follow instructions.
  - He called the intimidation claim ridiculous and said he does not get close to any employee since having COVID.
  - No union steward was available. Complainant was not told he could speak with his steward but had to leave immediately.
- *S1 (affidavit):*
  - She asked Complainant about three times to deliver his route, and he did not listen. He then became argumentative with PM.
  - She had no knowledge of events in the men's locker room.
  - No employee placed on EP was allowed to speak with the union before leaving the premises.

**Claim 2 (suspension, September 14, 2022)**
- *Complainant (affidavit):*
  - S1 and S2 approached him as he loaded his mail truck, and S2 demanded his badge.
  - S2 said he was being walked out for not fastening his seatbelt before starting the vehicle and for leaving the driver's seat with the engine running.
  - S2 denied his request for a union steward.
  - He understood Section 812 of Handbook M-41 to require seatbelts only while the vehicle is in motion.
  - He did not think age factored into this incident and had no comparator examples.
- *The record:*
  - Complainant was again placed on EP, off duty without pay.
  - He received a Notice of 14-Day Suspension on September 22, 2022. The letter cites failure to follow instructions on August 30, 2022 as the reason. ROI at 00192-00193.
- *S2 (affidavit):*
  - He observed Complainant exit the truck and walk in front of it with the engine running.
  - He called this a safety violation and said Agency policy requires seatbelts at all times while operating a vehicle.
  - Because Complainant was placed on EP immediately, he had to contact the union off postal property.
- *S1 (affidavit):* She had no knowledge of the incident because she was not present.

**Claim 3 (bathroom, September 20, 2022)**
- *Complainant (affidavit):*
  - S2 followed him into the bathroom twice, yelled at him, and threatened discipline.
  - He believed age was a factor because, being older, he has to use the bathroom more often.
  - He had no comparator examples.
- *S2 (affidavit):*
  - He denied raising his voice.
  - He said that if he followed Complainant, it was because of Complainant's performance.
  - Complainant spent a long time in the locker room doing something in his locker rather than washing up.

**Claim 4 (seatbelt, September 24, 2022)**
- *Complainant (affidavit):*
  - He started the engine and was fastening his seatbelt when S2 yelled at him through the passenger window.
  - Citing Section 812 of Handbook M-41, he said S2 wrongly required fastening before the engine is started rather than before the vehicle is shifted into gear.
  - S1 told S2 she saw nothing wrong.
  - He called the National Association of Letter Carriers (NALC) office, and someone there confirmed his understanding of the policy.
  - S1 told him to deliver his route, to follow all supervisor instructions, and to fasten his seatbelt before starting the engine from then on.
  - He did not think age was a factor and had no comparator examples.
- *S2 (affidavit):*
  - He thought seatbelts needed to be fastened before starting a vehicle.
  - He called safety and was told this was not a written Agency policy.
  - He told Complainant this, and Complainant was allowed to proceed on his route.
- *S1 (affidavit):*
  - She confirmed S2 called her over and asked whether she saw anything wrong. She did not, and she told Complainant to follow his supervisor's instructions.
  - She was unsure whether the request was sent to all carriers or whether other carriers already fastened seatbelts before starting.
  - She said the relevant conversation was between S2 and Complainant.

**Claim 5 (escorted out, November 1, 2022)**
- *Complainant (affidavit):*
  - He gave S1 a doctor's note for 30 days of no overtime due to right shoulder repetitive motion pain. S1 said she did not need to honor it.
  - That evening he returned with undelivered mail and clocked out. S1 told him to keep delivering until he finished.
  - He cited the note and said that ignoring it and demanding overtime did not seem safe.
  - S1 asked whether he was refusing instructions, then demanded his badge, and he was escorted off the premises.
  - He believed age was a factor because he was expected to finish an overburdened route, and as an older worker he recovers more slowly from pain and injury.
  - He had no comparator examples.
- *The record:* Complainant was again placed on EP, off duty without pay, effective November 2, 2022.
- *S1 (affidavit):*
  - Complainant told her, on union advice, that he could bring his mail back and did not have to listen to management.
  - She asked him three times to finish his route and told him he had to follow supervisor instruction.
  - She sent his medical documentation to Occupational Health Management (OHM), which advised that he could finish his route that day.
  - OHM said it was looking into whether the note had to be honored as a limited duty job offer or treated as a light duty request requiring PM approval, and told her to wait for an update.

## Decision and Reasoning
- **Decision-makers:**
  - The AJ decided the case without a hearing on January 4, 2024.
  - The Agency adopted and fully implemented that decision in its final order.
- **Outcome:** Complainant failed to prove the Agency subjected him to discrimination and harassment as alleged.
- **Criteria applied (as stated in the record):**
  - Whether the Agency's unrebutted facts established nondiscriminatory reasons for its actions.
  - Whether Complainant offered evidence of biased age-related comments by management or more favorable treatment of younger workers.
  - Whether, viewing the evidence in the light most favorable to Complainant, a reasonable factfinder could conclude the Agency's actions were tainted by age considerations.
- **Responses considered:**
  - The AJ noted, as examples, that Complainant argued with supervisors, wasted time on his phone in the locker room, neglected to fasten his seatbelt, and failed to turn off his vehicle when exiting.
  - The AJ found these predicates undisputed and a sufficient nondiscriminatory justification for the discipline and other management actions.
  - The AJ found no evidence of biased age comments or more favorable treatment of younger workers, so no reasonable factfinder could find age-based taint.

## Items to Note
- The only record citation in the source is ROI at 00192-00193, for the suspension notice. The other statements are attributed to affidavits without page cites.
- Claim 2 is framed as a September 14, 2022 suspension. The record shows the September 14 action was an EP, and the 14-day suspension notice was received September 22, 2022, citing the August 30 incident.
- The AJ's reference to phone use in the locker room does not appear in the affidavit summaries above. S2 described only Complainant spending a long time in the locker room and doing something in his locker.

# INVESTIGATION RECORD SUMMARY

**COMPLAINANT POSITION AND EMPLOYMENT:**
Complainant worked as a PSE Sales and Services Distribution Associate, Grade Level 06 P, at the Agency's Cape Central Post Office in Cape Coral, Florida.

**COMPLAINT FILING:**
On April 4, 2022, Complainant filed a formal EEO complaint claiming racial harassment based on her race ("White") when her first-line supervisor (Supervisor) (African American) made racial slurs and threatened to physically assault her, and when she informed management officials, they did nothing. (ROI, Affidavit A)

**ALLEGED INCIDENTS:**

Complainant stated during the investigation:
- **Late January/early February 2022:** Supervisor told her not to clock out for lunch due to overtime. When she asked if Supervisor would input her hours into the computer, he responded, "I'll slap the shit out of you." Later, when she asked if she could take her break, Supervisor responded, "people shouldn't be allowed breaks, Black people used to be slaves." (ROI, Affidavit A)

- **February 3, 2022:** When Complainant asked Supervisor for clarification of instructions, he responded, "I'll slap the shit out of you if you don't catch on." (ROI, Affidavit A)

- **February 5, 2022:** When Complainant told Supervisor a package was too heavy to lift, he responded she was "full of shit. You can't lift that?" (ROI, Affidavit A)

- **February 8, 2022:** After Complainant was instructed to bring the wagons around, Supervisor said, "You need to do it because you're White...." (ROI, Affidavit A)

- **February 24, 2022:** When Complainant said "huh?" after not hearing what Supervisor said, he responded, "What do you mean huh? I'll slap the shit out of you." (ROI, Affidavit A)

- **March 3, 2022:** While Complainant was walking out of the housekeeping closet after getting disposable gloves, Supervisor yelled, "White people don't steal, they buy their own shit." (ROI, Affidavit A)

Complainant stated she reported Supervisor's racial slurs and threats to the Manager, Customer Service (Manager) (Caucasian) and the union, but nothing was done. (ROI, Affidavit A)

**RESPONDENT SUPERVISOR'S STATEMENT:**
Supervisor unequivocally denied making any of the statements alleged by Complainant. He stated he believed they basically had a good working relationship until the complaint was filed. (ROI, Affidavit B)

**MANAGER'S STATEMENT:**
Manager affirmatively stated that Complainant never reported to her any of the comments allegedly made by Supervisor. (ROI, Affidavit C)

**SUPERVISOR 2'S STATEMENT:**
Another supervisor (Supervisor 2) (Caucasian) stated that Complainant once told him that Supervisor told her he would "slap her upside the head." He told her to report the matter to Manager. Supervisor 2 denied Complainant told him about any racial comments from Supervisor and asserted that Complainant told him she did not want to report the matter to Manager. (ROI, Affidavit D)

**CLAIM WITHDRAWAL:**
Complainant originally alleged unlawful retaliation but withdrew this claim during the investigation into her complaint, leaving only the racial harassment claim.

**AGENCY ACTION:**
Agency management has since apparently reassigned Complainant to a different supervisor. Complainant did not raise her reassignment as a claim.

**EEO INVESTIGATION AND NOTICE:**
After the EEO investigation, the Agency provided Complainant with a copy of the report of investigation and notice of her right to request a hearing before an EEOC Administrative Judge (AJ).

**ADMINISTRATIVE JUDGE HEARING:**
Complainant requested a hearing. However, Complainant did not respond to the AJ's October 24, 2022 order to submit preliminary case information and did not appear at the initial conference scheduled for November 24, 2022, as ordered by the AJ. On January 19, 2023, the AJ dismissed Complainant's hearing request and remanded the formal EEO complaint to the Agency for a final decision.

**FINAL DECISION:**
The Agency issued a final decision pursuant to 29 C.F.R. § 1614.110(b), finding no discrimination or unlawful retaliation was established as alleged.

**Case File Summary**

**Parties and position.** Complainant, who identifies as White, was a PSE Sales and Services Distribution Associate (Grade Level 06 P) at the Agency's Cape Central Post Office in Cape Coral, Florida. Her first-line supervisor (Supervisor) is African American. The Manager, Customer Service (Manager) is Caucasian, as is a second supervisor (Supervisor 2).

**Complaint.** On April 4, 2022, Complainant filed a formal EEO complaint alleging ongoing racial harassment (race: White). She claimed that in and around February 2022, Supervisor made racial slurs and threatened to physically assault her, and that management did nothing when she told them. The Agency accepted the complaint and investigated. She also originally alleged retaliation but withdrew that claim during the investigation, leaving only the harassment claim.

**Complainant's statements (ROI, Affidavit A).** Complainant said the following occurred:
- **Late January/early February 2022:** Supervisor told her not to clock out for lunch because of overtime. When she asked whether he would input her hours, he said, "I'll slap the shit out of you." When she later asked to take her break, he said, "people shouldn't be allowed breaks, Black people used to be slaves."
- **February 3, 2022:** When she asked for clarification of instructions, Supervisor said, "I'll slap the shit out of you if you don't catch on."
- **February 5, 2022:** When she said a package was too heavy to lift, Supervisor said she was "full of shit. You can't lift that?"
- **February 8, 2022:** After being told to bring the wagons around, she said Supervisor told her, "You need to do it because you're White...".
- **February 24, 2022:** When she said "huh?" because she did not hear him, Supervisor said, "What do you mean huh? I'll slap the shit out of you."
- **March 3, 2022:** As she left the housekeeping closet after getting disposable gloves, Supervisor yelled, "White people don't steal, they buy their own shit."
- **Reporting:** She said she reported the slurs and threats to Manager and to the union, but nothing was done.

**Responses considered.**
- **Supervisor (ROI, Affidavit B):** He unequivocally denied making any of the alleged statements. He said he believed they had a good working relationship until the complaint was filed.
- **Manager (ROI, Affidavit C):** She affirmatively stated that Complainant never reported any of the alleged comments to her.
- **Supervisor 2 (ROI, Affidavit D):** He stated that Complainant once told him Supervisor said he would "slap her upside the head," and that he told her to report it to Manager. He denied that she told him of any racial comments. He asserted that she told him she did not want to report the matter to Manager.

**Other facts.** Agency management has apparently since reassigned Complainant to a different supervisor. She did not raise the reassignment as a claim.

**Procedural history.**
- After the investigation, the Agency gave Complainant the report of investigation and notice of her right to request a hearing before an EEOC Administrative Judge (AJ). She requested a hearing.
- She did not respond to the AJ's October 24, 2022 order to submit preliminary case information. She also did not appear at the initial conference scheduled for November 24, 2022, as the AJ had ordered.
- On January 19, 2023, the AJ dismissed the hearing request and remanded the complaint to the Agency for a final decision.
- The Agency then issued a final decision under 29 C.F.R. § 1614.110(b). It found that no discrimination or unlawful retaliation was established as alleged. The record does not explain why retaliation was addressed given that Complainant had withdrawn that claim.
- Complainant then filed the instant appeal.

**Decision-makers.** The AJ dismissed the hearing request, and the Agency issued the final decision.

**Criteria applied.** The record cites only 29 C.F.R. § 1614.110(b) as the authority for the Agency's final decision. It does not state the substantive standard the Agency applied to the harassment claim. It also does not state the outcome of the appeal.

items.record:
**Case File Summary**

**Parties and position.** Complainant, who identifies as White, was a PSE Sales and Services Distribution Associate (Grade Level 06 P) at the Agency's Cape Central Post Office in Cape Coral, Florida. Her first-line supervisor (Supervisor) is African American. The Manager, Customer Service (Manager) is Caucasian, as is a second supervisor (Supervisor 2).

**Complaint.** On April 5, 2022, Complainant filed a formal EEO complaint alleging ongoing racial harassment (race: White). She claimed that in and around February 2022, Supervisor made racial slurs and threatened to physically assault her, and that management did nothing when she told them. The Agency accepted the complaint and investigated. She also originally alleged retaliation but withdrew that claim during the investigation, leaving only the harassment claim.

**Complainant's statements (ROI, Affidavit A).** Complainant said the following occurred:
- **Late January/early February 2022:** Supervisor told her not to clock out for lunch because of overtime. When she asked whether he would input her hours, he said, "I'll slap the shit out of you." When she later asked to take her break, he said, "people shouldn't be allowed breaks, Black people used to be slaves."
- **February 3, 2022:** When she asked for clarification of instructions, Supervisor said, "I'll slap the shit out of you if you don't catch on."
- **February 5, 2022:** When she said a package was too heavy to lift, Supervisor said she was "full of shit. You can't lift that?"
- **February 8, 2022:** After being told to bring the wagons around, she said Supervisor told her, "You need to do it because you're White...".
- **February 24, 2022:** When she said "huh?" because she did not hear him, Supervisor said, "What do you mean huh? I'll slap the shit out of you."
- **March 3, 2022:** As she left the housekeeping closet after getting disposable gloves, Supervisor yelled, "White people don't steal, they buy their own shit."
- **Reporting:** She said she reported the slurs and threats to Manager and to the union, but nothing was done.

**Responses considered.**
- **Supervisor (ROI, Affidavit B):** He unequivocally denied making any of the alleged statements. He said he believed they had a good working relationship until the complaint was filed.
- **Manager (ROI, Affidavit C):** She affirmatively stated that Complainant never reported any of the alleged comments to her.
- **Supervisor 2 (ROI, Affidavit D):** He stated that Complainant once told him Supervisor said he would "slap her upside the head," and that he told her to report it to Manager. He denied that she told him of any racial comments. He asserted that she told him she did not want to report the matter to Manager.

**Other facts.** Agency management has apparently since reassigned Complainant to a different supervisor. She did not raise the reassignment as a claim.

**Procedural history.**
- After the investigation, the Agency gave Complainant the report of investigation and notice of her right to request a hearing before an EEOC Administrative Judge (AJ). She requested a hearing.
- She did not respond to the AJ's October 24, 2022 order to submit preliminary case information. She also did not appear at the initial conference scheduled for November 24, 2022, as the AJ had ordered.
- On January 19, 2023, the AJ dismissed the hearing request and remanded the complaint to the Agency for a final decision.
- The Agency then issued a final decision under 29 C.F.R. § 1614.110(b). It found that no discrimination or unlawful retaliation was established as alleged. The record does not explain why retaliation was addressed given that Complainant had withdrawn that claim.
- Complainant then filed the instant appeal.

**Decision-makers.** The AJ dismissed the hearing request, and the Agency issued the final decision.

**Criteria applied.** The record cites only 29 C.F.R. § 1614.110(b) as the authority for the Agency's final decision. It does not state the substantive standard the Agency applied to the harassment claim. It also does not state the outcome of the appeal.

Complainant stated that she had previously filed an EEO complaint in September 2018, which remained pending before an EEOC Administrative Judge (AJ) at the time of her affidavit for the instant EEO complaint. See Report of Investigation (ROI) at 97. She explained that she suffers from post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression as a result of an incident where she was sexually harassed by a co-worker (the subject of her prior complaint), and that she also suffers from back, foot, and knee issues so she is unable to stand or walk for extended periods of time, cannot climb or descend stairs, and has restrictions on bending, stooping, and lifting. See ROI at 97-98. She also stated that due to the PTSD she suffers as a result of the co-worker’s sexual assault, her doctor stated that she can no longer work in the same facility as the co-worker who assaulted her. See ROI at 98-99. Complainant explained that the sexual harassment/assault occurred in September 2019 after which she went on Family & Medical Leave Act (FMLA) leave. See ROI at 100. She stated that she was released to return to work at a different facility from her harasser in April 2020, but when she arrived at work, her harasser was still there. See ROI at 100. She further alleged that in June 2020, she suffered a knee injury in the workplace, and she submitted documents to the Agency pertaining to her knee injury in July 2020, but received no response. See ROI at 100. She stated that the Agency’s Reasonable Accommodation Committee requested additional documentation which she had already provided and that they ignored her limitation resulting from her PTSD that required she be moved to a different facility from her harasser, instead focusing only on her physical restrictions due to her knee injury. See ROI at 100. She stated that in July 2021, she was finally given a modified assignment to a different location that accommodated her physical restrictions. 2 See ROI at 100. She went out on COVID leave on August 16, 2021, and then was later hospitalized for sepsis so she was ultimately not cleared to return to work until September 21, 2021. However, Complainant stated that she has not been returned to work because the Agency has refused to accommodate her restrictions, and she has only been told by management that there was no work available for her based on her restrictions. 3 See ROI at 100-105. There is no explanation or documentation in the record of Complainant’s new position or why it took the Agency a full year to move Complainant to a different work facility than her harasser. We emphasize that there is no statement from any Agency official confirming that any effort was made to accommodate Complainant’s restrictions from September 2021 onwards or that such an effort was unsuccessful. Complainant further alleged that she should not have been placed on leave without pay (LWOP) since November 21, 2021, because she was not able to work due to the Agency’s failure to accommodate her restrictions. In January 2022, she was denied a bid position, and the position was instead given to someone who had less seniority, while Complainant was marked “ineligible” with no explanation. 4 See ROI at 105; 108-9. EEO Complaint On May 13, 2022, Complainant filed an EEO complaint alleging that the Agency discriminated against her on the bases of race (African-American/Native American/Cuban), sex (female), color (Brown), disability (physical and mental), and reprisal for prior protected EEO activity under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Section 501 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 when: 1. Since November 10, 2021, she was not accommodated per her medical restrictions. 2. Since November 10, 2021, to present, she was charged LWOP. 3. On January 24, 2022, she was denied a bid position. 5 The Supervisor of Distribution Operations stated in her affidavit that Complainant’s bid was denied because she did not receive any updated medical documentation stating Complainant could fully perform her duties within 6 months. See ROI at 152. There is no evidence in the record indicating that Complainant was actually requested to provide such documentation or told she needed to do so as Complainant stated she was given no explanation for the denial. In addition, we note that the Collective Bargaining Agreement specifically states that in such a situation “management may, at the time of the submission of the bid or at any time thereafter, request that the employee provide medical certification indicating that the employee will be able to fully perform the duties of the bid for position within six months of the bid.” See ROI at 337. Complainant’s complaint also included three additional claims, specifically that between April 2020 and November 9, 2021, she was not accommodated per her medical restrictions; that on unspecified dates, her leave was not properly coded as workers’ compensation (OWCP) leave; and on unspecified dates, she was denied insurance benefits. Complainant had filed a motion to amend a pre-existing complaint to include her denial of reasonable accommodation claim for the period from April 2020 onwards but the AJ assigned to her other case denied the motion, finding that the denial of accommodation claim was not sufficiently like or related to her existing claim and noted that the time limits on EEO counseling be tolled from November 11, 2021, the date she filed the motion to amend. See ROI at 17-20. The Agency dismissed the denial of reasonable accommodation claim for the dates prior to November 10, 2021, pursuant to 29 C.F.R. §1614.107(a)(1) because of untimely counselor contact. See ROI at 62-63. The Agency also dismissed the claims regarding her leave not being properly coded and the denial of insurance benefits as collateral attacks on the workers’ compensation adjudicatory process. See ROI at 63-65. We find that the Agency’s affirmance of the claims regarding Complainant’s leave not being properly coded as OWCP leave and the denial of insurance benefits were On December 6, 2022, the Agency issued a final decision pursuant to 29 C.F.R. § 1614.110(b). The Agency found that Complainant did not submit required medical documentation to support her request for a reasonable accommodation or to show that she could perform the positions of her bid position within six months. The Agency also determined that Complainant did not demonstrate pretext for discrimination. The decision concluded that Complainant failed to prove that the Agency subjected her to discrimination as alleged. The instant appeal followed.
items.record:
# CASE FILE SUMMARY

**Complainant's Position and Medical History:**
At the time of the events giving rise to the complaint, Complainant worked as a Mail Processing Clerk at the Agency's Atlanta Processing and Distribution Center in Atlanta, Georgia. (ROI at 97)

Complainant stated she had previously filed an EEO complaint in September 2018, which remained pending before an EEOC Administrative Judge (AJ) at the time of her affidavit for the instant EEO complaint. (ROI at 97) Complainant stated she suffers from post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression as a result of an incident where she was sexually harassed by a co-worker (the subject of her prior complaint). (ROI at 97-98) She also suffers from back, foot, and knee issues so she is unable to stand or walk for extended periods of time, cannot climb or descend stairs, and has restrictions on bending, stooping, and lifting. (ROI at 97-98) Complainant stated that due to the PTSD she suffers as a result of the co-worker's sexual assault, her doctor stated that she can no longer work in the same facility as the co-worker who assaulted her. (ROI at 98-99)

**Timeline of Events:**

Complainant explained that the sexual harassment/assault occurred in September 2019 after which she went on Family & Medical Leave Act (FMLA) leave. (ROI at 100) She stated that she was released to return to work at a different facility from her harasser in April 2020, but when she arrived at work, her harasser was still there. (ROI at 100)

Complainant alleged that in June 2020, she suffered a knee injury in the workplace, and she submitted documents to the Agency pertaining to her knee injury in July 2020, but received no response. (ROI at 100) She stated that the Agency's Reasonable Accommodation Committee requested additional documentation which she had already provided and that they ignored her limitation resulting from her PTSD that required she be moved to a different facility from her harasser, instead focusing only on her physical restrictions due to her knee injury. (ROI at 100)

She stated that in July 2021, she was finally given a modified assignment to a different location that accommodated her physical restrictions. (ROI at 100) She went out on COVID leave on August 16, 2021, and then was later hospitalized for sepsis so she was ultimately not cleared to return to work until September 21, 2021. (ROI at 100-105) However, Complainant stated that she has not been returned to work because the Agency has refused to accommodate her restrictions, and she has only been told by management that there was no work available for her based on her restrictions. (ROI at 100-105)

Complainant further alleged that she should not have been placed on leave without pay (LWOP) since November 21, 2021, because she was not able to work due to the Agency's failure to accommodate her restrictions. (ROI at 100-105) In January 2022, she was denied a bid position, and the position was instead given to someone who had less seniority, while Complainant was marked "ineligible" with no explanation. (ROI at 105; 108-9)

**EEO Complaint Filed:**
On May 13, 2022, Complainant filed an EEO complaint alleging that the Agency discriminated against her on the bases of race (African-American/Native American/Cuban), sex (female), color (Brown), disability (physical and mental), and reprisal for prior protected EEO activity under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Section 501 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 when:

1. Since November 10, 2021, she was not accommodated per her medical restrictions.
2. Since November 10, 2021, to present, she was charged LWOP.
3. On January 24, 2022, she was denied a bid position.

(ROI at 105; 108-9)

**Agency Response to Bid Denial:**
The Supervisor of Distribution Operations stated in her affidavit that Complainant's bid was denied because she did not receive any updated medical documentation stating Complainant could fully perform her duties within 6 months. (ROI at 152) The record contains no evidence indicating that Complainant was actually requested to provide such documentation or told she needed to do so, as Complainant stated she was given no explanation for the denial. The Collective Bargaining Agreement specifically states that "management may, at the time of the submission of the bid or at any time thereafter, request that the employee provide medical certification indicating that the employee will be able to fully perform the duties of the bid for position within six months of the bid." (ROI at 337)

**Additional Claims:**
Complainant's complaint also included three additional claims: (1) between April 2020 and November 9, 2021, she was not accommodated per her medical restrictions; (2) on unspecified dates, her leave was not properly coded as workers' compensation (OWCP) leave; and (3) on unspecified dates, she was denied insurance benefits.

Complainant had filed a motion to amend a pre-existing complaint to include her denial of reasonable accommodation claim for the period from April 2020 onwards but the AJ assigned to her other case denied the motion, finding that the denial of accommodation claim was not sufficiently like or related to her existing claim and noted that the time limits on EEO counseling be tolled from November 11, 2021, the date she filed the motion to amend. (ROI at 17-20)

**Agency Dismissals:**
The Agency dismissed the denial of reasonable accommodation claim for the dates prior to November 10, 2021, pursuant to 29 C.F.R. §1614.107(a)(1) because of untimely counselor contact. (ROI at 62-63) The Agency also dismissed the claims regarding her leave not being properly coded and the denial of insurance benefits as collateral attacks on the workers' compensation adjudicatory process. (ROI at 63-65)

**Final Agency Decision:**
On December 6, 2022, the Agency issued a final decision pursuant to 29 C.F.R. § 1614.110(b). The Agency found that Complainant did not submit required medical documentation to support her request for a reasonable accommodation or to show that she could perform the positions of her bid position within six months. The Agency also determined that Complainant did not demonstrate pretext for discrimination. The decision concluded that Complainant failed to prove that the Agency subjected her to discrimination as alleged.

**Appeal:**
The instant appeal followed the Agency's final decision of December 6, 2022.
